That is a user-visible defect today, and RFC 3339 fixes it.

nodes.label: The canonical companion timestamp is RFC 3339 at fixed second resolution
nodes.norm_label: the canonical companion timestamp is rfc 3339 at fixed second resolution
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - f6-unify-companion-timestamps [ses_f0647ee26ffeQpUdPkO43mYL1M].md:L4514] `parseCompanionTimestamp` has a special case that exists *solely* to repair the space form: it regex-matches `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` and rewrites it to `+ "Z"` before handing it to `new Date()`.

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - f6-unify-companion-timestamps [ses_f0647ee26ffeQpUdPkO43mYL1M].md:L4518] Nanoseconds are variable-width: `2026-05-19T10:00:00Z` sorts *after* `2026-05-19T10:00:00.123456789Z` because `.` (0x2E) < `Z` (0x5A), which would reintroduce the identical bug one character position later.
